findings.evidence:
`OrderResponse.status` becomes `OrderResponse.state`; the old name is not
kept. The OpenAPI file is regenerated.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: The field is renamed in place
findings.recommendation: The design's own context says "partners' integrations read `status` to know when to ship": on the day this ships, every partner integration calling `GET /orders/{id}` reads `status` as undefined (it is also `required` in `openapi.yaml`, so schema-validating clients reject the response) and stops shipping orders, with no warning. Use expand then contract: return both `state` and `status` (marked `deprecated: true` in `openapi.yaml`) for a stated deprecation period, then remove `status` in a later change. Add a requirement and a scenario to `specs/orders-api/spec.md` that `status` is still returned with the same value during that period, and a task in `tasks.md` that tests it — today the only tasks and scenarios cover `state` alone, so no migration path is tested.
findings.title: The public `status` field is removed with no deprecation period

findings.evidence: - Changed: The order's `status` field is now called `state`.
findings.recommendation: Renaming a field of the public `GET /orders/{id}` response breaks every consumer that reads `status`, yet the note reads as an ordinary change, so partners reading it get no signal to act before their integrations fail. Mark the item **BREAKING**, state what consumers must do (read `state` instead of `status`) and by when the old field disappears if a deprecation period is kept (see R-migration-1).
findings.title: The release note does not mark the rename as BREAKING nor say what partners must do
